02 • CASE SELECTOR

Choose a case. Read the scenario, write your prediction, then reveal the model answer.

🏃 400-m Runner

03 • CASE 1 — 400-m RUNNER

400-m runner • very high demand • rapid ATP support + substantial glycolytic contribution
CASE 1 • 400 m

Very high intensity

Age: 20 • Event: 400 m • Demand: very high intensity

Question 1: Predict the relative contribution of ATP-PCr, glycolytic and oxidative pathways.
Model: All three contribute. ATP-PCr supports the rapid start; glycolytic contribution becomes substantial as the effort continues; oxidative contribution is present and rises over time.
Question 2: Why may lactate rise?
Model: High glycolytic flux increases pyruvate production. Lactate formation can accompany rapid NAD⁺ regeneration, and blood lactate can rise when lactate appearance exceeds immediate utilisation/clearance.

04 • CASE 2 — 5-km RUNNER

CASE 2 • 5 KM

Sustained high aerobic demand

Age: 24 • Event: 5 km • Demand: sustained high aerobic demand

Question: What changes in substrate contribution and oxygen consumption as pace increases?
Model: Oxidative metabolism provides a large share of ATP, while glycolytic and phosphagen pathways still contribute. As pace/intensity rises, carbohydrate contribution generally increases and VO₂ rises toward the athlete's upper capacity.

05 • CASE 3 — 2-HOUR RIDE

2-hour ride • oxidative support • carbohydrate + fat both contribute
CASE 3 • 2-HOUR RIDE

Prolonged endurance exercise

Scenario: moderate endurance cycling with limited carbohydrate intake.

Question: Predict what happens to substrate contribution as duration progresses.
Model: Oxidative metabolism dominates. Fat oxidation can contribute substantially, while carbohydrate remains important. With prolonged duration and declining glycogen availability, maintaining high intensity becomes more difficult.

06 • CASE 4 — INTERVAL TRAINING

CASE 4 • 10 × 30 s

Why does recovery quality affect the next interval?

Scenario: 10 × 30 s hard efforts with 90 s recovery.

Question: Why can the next interval feel different from the first even when the work duration is the same?
Model: Recovery allows partial PCr resynthesis, lactate/metabolite handling and cardiovascular/respiratory recovery. Incomplete recovery changes the starting state of the next interval, so the same external workload may produce a different internal response.

07 • COMPARE THE CASES

400 mVery high demandATP-PCr + substantial glycolytic + oxidative present
5 kmSustained high demandOxidative large share + other pathways contribute
2-hour rideProlonged demandOxidative dominant; CHO + fat both contribute
IntervalsRepeated high demandRecovery changes the next interval's starting state

08 • DON'T JUST MEMORISE — BUILD YOUR OWN CASE ANSWER

Write a 5-sentence physiology answer.

Sentence 1 → State the exercise demand.
Sentence 2 → Identify relevant fuel(s).
Sentence 3 → Explain the relative pathway contribution.
Sentence 4 → Name measurements that could provide evidence.
Sentence 5 → Explain the recovery implication.

Model structure: “The exercise demand determines the required rate and duration of ATP supply. Available substrates influence which fuels can support the demand. ATP-PCr, glycolytic and oxidative pathways contribute together, but their relative contribution changes with the task. HR, VO₂, VCO₂, RER, lactate, RPE and external workload can provide evidence in appropriate contexts. After exercise stops, recovery processes restore PCr, handle lactate/metabolites and restore energy stores over different time scales.”

10 • HIGH-YIELD TAKE-HOME

CASE-BASED LEARNING = REASON, DON'T RECITE.

Start with the demand → identify fuel availability → explain relative pathway contribution → consider ATP regeneration rate → choose measurements → interpret in context → explain recovery.
NOW YOU KNOW → NEXT: Next, use physiological datasets to READ THE PHYSIOLOGY and interpret patterns rather than just numbers.
